Behavioral function refers to the types of reinforcement a behavior is maintained by - knowing what reinforces a behavior allows a BCBA to modify the environment so that more desirable forms of behavior contact those reinforcers, while less / undesirable behavior does not contact those reinforcers.

Behavioral function is specific to the analysis of children with a diagnosis of ASD. Children with autism are very rigid and stereotyped and frequently fall into four categories of behavior: sensory, escape, tangible item access, and adult attention (S.E.A.T.).

Behavioral function is a myth - humans are complex organisms, and as such, no gestalt "reason" exists for the myriad behaviors people engage in. We can at best suppose rationales for our decisions as the product of the constant struggle between the Id, Ego, and Superego which form the basis of all human personality.

Behavioral function is an algorithm used to calculate the probability of human behavior(s) by plugging in their GPS coordinates, favorite reinforcers, known punishers, etc. into a supercomputer system, such as Alexa, Siri, Watson, or Google. These devices then analyze your behavior and reveal to you the best way to advertise to a person.

The RBT doesn't spend enough time with clients to stand much of a chance at identifying behavioral function; they should leave that up to the client's family and other caregivers.

The RBT spends a significant amount of time with the client and has some training in the basics of behavioral function.
